q: How does an NGO or trust work out its carbon footprint?
title: Carbon footprint for an NGO
short: The same way a company does. Under operational control, count fuel for your vehicles and generators as Scope 1 and electricity in your offices and centres as Scope 2. Add staff travel and major purchases as Scope 3. Donors mostly want a clear, sourced figure and what you plan to change.

ul: Electricity bills for every office, school or clinic you run.
Programmes run by partners: their emissions are theirs, unless you control the site.
Donated goods: count only if you choose to include them, and say how.

senseible: Senseible reads electricity bills (CEA grid factor 0.710 kg CO2 per kWh, CO2 Baseline Database version 21.0) and diesel, LPG and gas invoices (IPCC 2006 defaults) into a dated, fingerprinted Scope 1 and 2 record for each site, and labels estimates as estimates.

sources.label: GHG Protocol Corporate Value Chain (Scope 3) Standard
